cluster_summary: A collection of vulnerabilities where user-controlled environment variable overrides are passed to subprocesses without adequate sanitization. The code lacks comprehensive blocklists or allowlists for dangerous variables (e.g., LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS, SHELLOPTS, HOME) that can alter process execution, bypass security controls, or lead to arbitrary code injection. Fixes involve adding centralized sanitization functions that block or allowlist specific variables depending on context.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Validate environment variable names and values to reject any containing newline characters (CR or LF) before insertion into the unit file..

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Validate environment variable names and values to reject any containing newline characters (CR or LF) before insertion into the unit file.
sub_patterns.name: Missing newline validation in systemd unit file injection
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled environment variable values are embedded into systemd unit file templates without stripping or rejecting newline characters (CR/LF), allowing an attacker to break out of the Environment= directive and inject arbitrary systemd configuration directives.
